title: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
abstract: We establish an equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors. The classical sampler--extractor equivalence is established by a seminal work of Zuckerman (Random Structures & Algorithms, 1997).   Using this equivalence, we construct explicit strong matrix samplers with optimal randomness overhead and near-optimal sample complexity via constructing quantum-proof extractors. Specifically for matrix dimension $D$, accuracy $\varepsilon$ and failure probability $δ\leq\varepsilon$, our matrix sampler uses $m+O_α(\log(D/δ))$ random bits and $O_α(\varepsilon^{-2-α}\log^{1+α}(D/δ))$ samples, for any constant $α>0$. Compared with the matrix sampler of Xun and Zuckerman (CCC 2025), our construction has improvements in two aspects. Under the same optimal random seed length, we can replace the $\operatorname{poly} D$ dependence in the number of samples by $O(\log^{1-γ} D)$. Under the same scale of sample size, we can remove their $\log\log D$ factor in the length of the random seed. Our underlying strong quantum-proof extractor has output length $n-O_α(a+\log(1/η))$ and seed length at most $(1+α)\log a+(2+α)\log(1/η)+O_α(1)$ for $n$-bit sources with conditional min-entropy $n-a$ and error $η$.   We also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors for every constant entropy rate, for any error as small as $2^{-Ω(n)}$, having optimal seed length $O(\log(n/η))$ and output length $Ω(n)$, improving previous constructions.
summary: This paper proves a deep equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors. It then constructs highly efficient, explicit versions of these tools, significantly improving the known resource bounds for both sampling and randomness extraction. This advances the theoretical understanding of how randomness can be efficiently extracted and utilized in quantum information tasks.
main_problem: The paper establishes a formal equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors, aiming to construct explicit, near-optimal versions of both tools.
main_result: They provide explicit constructions for strong matrix samplers and quantum-proof extractors, significantly improving resource bounds compared to prior work.
method: The work relies on establishing a theoretical correspondence between the two concepts and then employing advanced techniques from quantum information theory, such as bounding trace distance and utilizing conditional min-entropy.
model_or_system: The context is abstract information theory, dealing with random sampling of matrices (estimators for expected values) and the extraction of randomness from noisy quantum sources.

important_parameters: Dimension ($D$), accuracy ($\epsilon$), failure probability ($\delta$), and entropy rate ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The equivalence is built upon classical results (Zuckerman, 1997) and quantum security analysis requiring bounds on conditional min-entropy.
